headline: High: shared-bus Pipecat can feed Slim untrusted content, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pipecat’s shared bus and stdin/stdout can pass agent outputs into Slim’s interactive CLI or command execution path. Slim reads filesystem artifacts and executes shell commands, so attacker-controlled text from Pipecat can be treated as instructions if bridged into prompts or scripts. This is an interaction risk for both agents, not a proven exploit.
conditions: IF Pipecat output is copied into Slim prompts or shell commands, injection is possible.
IF an orchestrator forwards shared-bus text into Slim without sanitization, instructions can be hijacked.
mitigations: Use a strict delimiter/escaping wrapper for any text passed between agents.
Disable copy-paste bridging for operator workflows.
Add a one-line provenance tag to all inter-agent messages.
Review Slim commands before execution for embedded instructions.
requires-engineering: add structured message schemas and parser hardening.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Pipecat touches audio, video, images, text, and conversation state, while Slim reads filesystem artifacts and handles certificate private keys and registry credentials. If Pipecat shares a workspace or forwards transcripts/files into Slim, sensitive data can be exposed and then transmitted via Slim’s broad network egress. The pair creates a realistic leakage path in default-style integrations.
conditions: IF Pipecat stores transcripts or media in a shared workspace, Slim can read them.
IF Slim is pointed at directories containing secrets or credentials, those contents may be exfiltrated over broad egress.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and mount only least-privilege paths.
Keep secrets out of any directory Slim scans.
Rotate any registry credentials used in the same environment.
Audit Pipecat outputs for sensitive media before handoff.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation and egress policy.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Pipecat supports shared-bus multi-instance operation, while Slim has write_filesystem, execute_shell, and spawn_subprocesses. If both are wired to the same mutable directory or artifact set, they can overwrite each other’s files or race on generated outputs. The profiles do not prove a shared directory, so uncertainty keeps this below high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF Pipecat and Slim share mutable artifacts without locking, race conditions can corrupt outputs.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent.
Make shared artifacts read-only for one side.
Use file locks around any shared writes.
Check timestamps before overwriting generated files.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking and conflict detection.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pipecat can generate conversational text and analytics, and Slim can act through shell execution and filesystem writes. If Slim treats Pipecat output as authoritative, a mistaken transcript or hallucinated instruction can cascade into incorrect container changes or deletions. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly documented, so uncertainty stays at medium.
conditions: IF Slim consumes Pipecat output without verification, errors can propagate into actions.
IF Pipecat emits malformed or hallucinated instructions, Slim may execute them.
mitigations: Require human review before any Slim action.
Add a verification step that checks Pipecat output against policy.
Use allowlisted commands only.
Log and diff all proposed filesystem changes.
requires-engineering: implement typed handoff contracts between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Pipecat processes audio/video/text conversation data, while Slim handles filesystem artifacts, certificate private keys, and registry credentials. If regulated content such as personal audio or secrets is routed from Pipecat into Slim’s temporary container or logs, retention and residency controls may diverge. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so this remains medium.
conditions: IF regulated audio or text is forwarded from Pipecat into Slim logs or artifacts, retention may diverge.
IF the deployment stores Pipecat conversation state alongside Slim outputs, deletion/export obligations may conflict.
mitigations: Classify data before handoff and block regulated fields.
Set short log retention for both agents.
Keep secrets out of shared artifacts.
Document a deletion/export workflow for combined outputs.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across the pair.
